deep.reconstruction:
The page contains no words, numbers or formulas. It is a single drawing. The sheet is divided by ruled ink lines into a 2 x 3 grid of rectangles.

Four rectangles are filled with small hand-drawn circles ('o'): upper left, upper right, middle left and lower left. The lower-right region (the bottom two thirds of the right half) is empty. The machine transcription says 'three rectangles' but then lists four; the image shows four filled blocks.

Within each block the circles form a regular, doubly periodic pattern. They run in slanting diagonal rows, with neighbouring circles roughly 20-25 px apart horizontally. In the upper-left block, the columns near x ~ 110, 133, 155, 182, 207, 230, 255 and 278 each repeat with a vertical period of about 190 px. The pattern also repeats horizontally with a period of about 193 px; for example, the column at x ~ 303 repeats the one at x ~ 110. That suggests a near-square repeat cell containing about 8 points.

My rough pixel estimates are too noisy to decide two things: whether the points form an exact two-dimensional lattice (a set {m*a + n*b}) or only a periodic arrangement of 8 points per cell; and whether the four blocks show the same pattern or variants. The upper-right block looks like the same kind of pattern, with slightly different spacing near its edges.

There is no derivation to reconstruct.

Possible purposes, all conjectural (mine):
(a) visualising a point lattice, as in Gauss's geometric treatment of binary/ternary quadratic forms (Disquisitiones; Seeber review 1831);
(b) counting points in a region to estimate area, i.e. number of points ~ area / cell area;
(c) displaying graphically some residue pattern, of the kind tabulated on the following leaf.

The next page (f.37) holds a 5-digit numerical table with columns 0-9. Its first row is consistent with 100000 - 500k^2 + k for k = 1..9 (e.g. 99501, 98002, ..., 59509). This hints at a computational, perhaps residue-based, context, but nothing on this page ties the drawing to that table.
